ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *(H)yéh₁kt ~ *(H)ih₁kéntder. Latin iaciō Proto-Indo-European *-tus Proto-Italic *-tus Latin -tus Latin iactus Vulgar Latin *iectus Old French get French jetbor. English jet Borrowed from French jet (“spurt”, literally “a throw”), from Old French get, giet, from Vulgar Latin *iectus, *jectus, from Latin iactus (“a throwing, a throw”), from iacere (“to throw”). See abject, ejaculate, gist, jess, jut. Cognate with Spanish echar.

chain.g: A hard, black asphalt; variety of lignite; jet, jess.

ety.text: From Middle English get, geet, gete, from a northern form of Old French jayet, jaiet, gaiet, from Latin gagātēs, from Ancient Greek Γαγάτης (Gagátēs), from Γάγας (Gágas, “a town and river in Lycia”). Doublet of gagate.

senses.d: A collimated stream, spurt or flow of liquid or gas from a pressurized container, an engine, etc.
A spout or nozzle for creating a jet of fluid.
A type of airplane using jet engines rather than propellers.
A turbine.
A rocket engine.
A part of a carburetor that controls the amount of fuel mixed with the air.
A narrow cone of hadrons and other particles produced by the hadronization of a quark or gluon.
Drift; scope; range, as of an argument.
The sprue of a type, which is broken from it when the type is cold.
To spray out of a container.
To spray with liquid from a container.
ex: Farmers may either dip or jet sheep with chemicals.

senses.d: To travel on a jet aircraft or otherwise by jet propulsion
To move (running, walking etc.) rapidly around
To shoot forward or out; to project; to jut out.
To strut; to walk with a lofty or haughty gait; to be insolent; to obtrude.
ex:
Why, lords, and think you not how dangerous
It is to jet upon a prince’s right?
Contemplation makes a rare turkey-cock of him: how he jets under his advanced plumes!

senses.d: To jerk; to jolt; to be shaken.
To adjust the fuel to air ratio of a carburetor; to install or adjust a carburetor jet
To leave; depart.
Propelled by turbine engines.
A hard, black form of coal, sometimes used in jewellery.
ex: There is also a factitious jeat made of glaſs, in imitation of the mineral jeat.

senses.d: The colour of jet coal, deep grey.
Very dark black in colour.
ex: She was an ash blonde with greenish eyes, beaded lashes, hair waved smoothly back from ears in which large jet buttons glittered.

senses.d: an operation that takes a differentiable function f and produces a polynomial, the Taylor polynomial (truncated Taylor series) of f, at each point of its domain.
